> [!TLDR] Where we are
> Every decision from the original review is shipped. The kit ships ~50 chart types, table popover + per-column filter + multi-column sort, smart-hide chrome, mermaid hover/tooltip/click parity, lightbox pan-zoom, and a JSON authoring surface that AI can emit. Plot family is on the canonical `mark + encoding + data` shape; aliases preserved. Open-questions table is empty of actionable items; library adoption stays deferred until a concrete renderer gap appears.
>
> - **Shipped:** code → output label rename, function-grouped chart picker, smart-quiet chrome on charts/tables/diagrams/code blocks, live chart-config popover (type · marks · mode · arc · orientation), table gear popover (view · group-by · per-column filter · multi-column sort), Cmd/Ctrl+click solo on legends.
> - **Chart inventory (~50 types):** plot family (scatter/line/area), arc family (donut/pie), bar family (single/stacked/grouped, horizontal/vertical), distribution family (histogram/box-plot/violin/candlestick — each with orientation switch), relationship family (chord/network/sankey/scatter-matrix/parallel-coordinates), hierarchy (treemap/sunburst), part-to-whole (waffle/polar-area/marimekko), Cartesian extras (bubble/quadrant/connected-scatter), time series (sparkline/calendar-heatmap/stream/bump/horizon), comparison (slope/dumbbell/lollipop/waterfall), other (gauge/bullet/radar/dot-plot/density/beeswarm/funnel/gantt/tile-map/population-pyramid/hexbin/small-multiples).
> - **Curve shapes:** line/area gained `curve: "smooth"` (Catmull-Rom). Distribution charts have orientation switches.
> - **Mermaid parity:** hover-neighbour highlight on flowcharts, kit-styled tooltip + `→ url` footer via `click NodeId href "url" "tooltip"`, hover-lift across every diagram type (flowchart / sequence / state / class / ER / gantt / pie / journey / mindmap / timeline / sankey).
> - **Test surface:** 335 content-regression tests pin every load-bearing piece. `oku check` clean across 20 doc pages.
> - **Deferred by user:** library adoption revisit. The kit's own renderers cover the catalog.

> [!INFO] Test surface
> 335 content-regression tests pin every load-bearing pattern. `oku check` runs schema + structural + content checks before every build. Browser sweeps via Playwright on each landing; the bounding-box numbers go into the commit message.

## The north star {#north-star}

Restate the contract so every later decision is measured against it. (Unchanged from the original review.)

> [!INFO] Contract (from the user, paraphrased)
> JSON is the substrate so AI can read / write / modify content without fighting style or glue markup. The presentation should be capable yet simple — simplicity is the ultimate sophistication. Pre-defined structures should be enough for the 90% case, but raw HTML/JS escape hatches should remain available for the 10%.

Two failure modes to guard against. **Drift toward complexity:** every new feature adds schema surface, runtime branches, and visual-language vocabulary the reader has to learn. Each addition is locally justifiable; collectively they erode the contract. **Drift toward purity:** rejecting every addition leaves the reader with bullet-points and tables for everything a chart could illustrate. Equally a failure.

The discipline: every new primitive must answer two questions. **(1) Can AI emit this in one obvious shape, with no per-page judgement calls?** (2) Does the rendered result earn the schema cost — i.e., does the reader recognise the shape faster than they'd parse a paragraph + bullets?

## What's still open {#open-questions}

Decisions or design questions outstanding after this round.

rows: Orientation switch for SVG charts (violin / box-plot / histogram / candlestick)

Each chart's default orientation is unchanged; `orientation` attribute opt-in dispatches to a sibling renderer. Histogram → horizontal bins; box-plot → vertical columns; violin → vertical columns; candlestick → horizontal (time on Y).
mermaid v10's `click NodeId href "url" "tooltip"` now uses the kit's `.okc-tooltip` rendering with a `→ <url>` footer; click navigation continues via mermaid's existing `<a xlink:href>` wrapping.
Arc + bar (Q31/Q32); plot was already done. Q36 also added DIV-bar toolbar so the popover is now reachable architecturally.

Decision: categorical / flow families don't benefit from a forced dual-form unification. Plot/arc/bar all share underlying data shape across their alternates (same series → different marks; same slices → pie vs donut; same series → single vs stacked vs grouped). Categorical types (heatmap.cells vs waffle.segments vs treemap.tree) have intrinsically different payloads — a unification would be sugar without substance. Skipped; can revisit if a real cross-type compatibility emerges.
population-pyramid + connected-scatter (Q33), horizon + hexbin (Q37/Q38), small multiples (Q41). Catalogue gaps closed; new additions should be driven by concrete reader needs.
Fold markers + sidebar collapse handle were already smart-hide in round 1; Q34 added language-pill smart-hide; Q39 added bar toolbar smart-hide parity. No outstanding items.
Re-ask when there is a concrete pain the kit's own renderers can't address. The kit ships ~50 chart types now, none requiring an external library.

## Risk register (updated) {#risk-register}

What could go wrong with the pending work.

rows: Existing pages emit `scatter` / `line` / `area` / `stacked-bar` / `grouped-bar` / `pie` / `donut`. If aliases break, all 18 doc pages fail to render.

Aliases are non-negotiable, not optional. Test matrix: every old type name must produce the same DOM as before. Schema accepts both old and new; renderer normalises. Tests: existing chart-content regression tests already cover this surface.
Reader switches to a mark the data doesn't actually support (e.g. line on categorical x).
`compatible_with` is author-declared, not auto-inferred. Author opts in only when they've checked the data shape. UI hides the toggle when only one option exists.
Hidden chrome makes affordances undiscoverable — first-time visitors don't know there's a filter input on the table.
Default opacity is 0.15, not 0. Affordance is visible but quiet — a hint, not a hide. Force-show on active state means the user never loses sight of state they've already set.
Each new chart type expands the schema and the runtime. Adding all 15 from the gap list would re-introduce the drift the north star guards against.

Add one at a time, each with a written justification against the two north-star questions. Sunburst is high-value (different hierarchy view); pictograms are low-value (a styling variant of waffle). Discriminate.
